s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive purpura and ecchymoses with systemic involvement
salient_findings: Waxy yellow papules and plaques with purpura
Anemia, abnormal liver function test results, and renal impairment
Amorphous eosinophilic deposits on hematoxylin-eosin staining
Positive Congo red staining and apple-green birefringence
key_facts: 1-year history of purpura, ecchymoses, anorexia, and weight loss
Medical history of alcohol abuse and cognitive impairment
Purpura and ecchymoses initially periorbital, progressed over 12 months
Elder abuse excluded
Anemia, abnormal liver function test results, and renal impairment with moderate proteinuria
Normal serum protein electrophoresis (SPEP) and immunofixation urine protein electrophoresis test results
Unremarkable radiological studies
4-mm punch biopsy showed upper dermal amorphous eosinophilic deposits
Congo red staining results were positive
Polarizing light microscopy demonstrated pale apple-green birefringence

shortlist.label: Systemic amyloidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Positive Congo red staining and apple-green birefringence on biopsy, consistent with amyloid deposits

shortlist.label: Primary systemic (AL) amyloidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of purpura, ecchymoses, and systemic involvement, with normal SPEP and immunofixation results

shortlist.label: Lipoid proteinosis
shortlist.why_kept: Waxy yellow papules and plaques with purpura, similar to those seen in lipoid proteinosis

shortlist.label: Multiple myeloma-associated amyloidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Anemia and renal impairment, which can be associated with multiple myeloma and amyloidosis

shortlist.label: Secondary systemic amyloidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic disease and inflammation, which can lead to secondary amyloidosis

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms, including purpura, ecchymoses, anorexia, and weight loss, along with the biopsy findings of upper dermal amorphous eosinophilic deposits, positive Congo red staining, and pale apple-green birefringence under polarizing light microscopy, are consistent with systemic amyloidosis. The absence of abnormal serum protein electrophoresis (SPEP) and immunofixation urine protein electrophoresis test results makes Primary systemic (AL) amyloidosis and Multiple myeloma-associated amyloidosis less likely.

rejected.label: Primary systemic (AL) amyloidosis
rejected.why: Normal SPEP and immunofixation urine protein electrophoresis test results

rejected.label: Multiple myeloma-associated amyloidosis
rejected.why: Normal SPEP and immunofixation urine protein electrophoresis test results

rejected.label: Lipoid proteinosis
rejected.why: Clinical presentation and biopsy findings are not consistent with lipoid proteinosis

rejected.label: Secondary systemic amyloidosis
rejected.why: No clear evidence of chronic infection or inflammation
